statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: Most quests of level 48 and higher now also pay gold. This came in the 10 Nov hotfixes. Excluded are quests that already give valuable items, repeatable quests, and trivial quests. No per-quest amounts were published.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: Forever deliberately drops the original level-60 conversion of quest XP into gold. Blizzard's reason is that it would reward hoarding finished quests until 60.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: Only about 25% of original quests paid raw gold, so removing the conversion cut late-level income more than intended. Gold rewards do not grow further at 60.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: A streamer reported a developer hint about a weekly quest at 60 that pays random gold. This is unconfirmed.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: The 10 Nov hotfixes announced that the AH minimum deposit would drop from 1 silver to 1 copper. They also fixed AH mail that arrived after about 2 minutes instead of the intended 60, and the wrong sender name on that mail.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: On 12 Nov Blizzard pulled the AH changes and rescheduled them for the 17 Nov US maintenance (18 Nov in EU).

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: The official 17 Nov hotfix notes have no AH entry, so as of 18 Nov the 1-copper minimum is not officially confirmed live. A Wowhead headline says it was reduced, but its body could not be read.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text:
Vendor sell prices for crafted goods were cut repeatedly to stop people crafting just to sell to vendors:
– 1 Oct: crafted wands sell for 1c.
– 8 Oct: many Enchanting items and Peace Tea were lowered.
– 16 Oct: many profession-made items were lowered.
– 5 Nov: Mild Spices went to 1c.
– 10 Nov: Minor Arcane Elixir went to 5c, Iron Grenade to 1s25c, and some crafted Bind-on-Pickup armour from Blacksmithing, Leatherworking and Tailoring was also cut.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: Racial vendor mounts became Bind-on-Pickup on 10 Nov, so they cannot be bought for other players or resold.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: Since 9 Nov, XP from dungeon kills is up 50%, and Waylaid Crates and Craftsman's Writs can drop in dungeons. Since 13 Nov, party members get no XP from dungeon kills that are trivial for their level.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: The repeatable "Water Pouch Bounty" quest gives no XP (16 Nov), and Shatterspear Trolls give no XP (10 Nov).

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: "Temporary Economy Holds" let Blizzard restrict trade, mail, guild bank and AH access on accounts suspected of real-money trading (buying or selling gold for cash) while they investigate. The hold lifts automatically if the account is cleared.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: GDKP raids (where players bid gold for loot) are not allowed in Forever, and action against gold buying and selling is more aggressive.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: Forever has no WoW Token, so gold must be earned in the game.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: The Item Restoration service was disabled on 11 Nov while a bug is investigated.

statements.title: Forever economy changes log (official)
statements.text: A reported Blackmaw Hold loot farm (100+ gold per hour) stopped dropping loot around 16 Nov. One aggregator headline says exploiters were penalised. None of this is in official notes, but the coach should steer users away from exploit farms.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: The gold cost of riding moved from the mount to riding training, as in the later TBC model, and you receive a mount when you learn the skill. Blizzard has published no gold figure.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Apprentice Riding is available at level 40 for 100g, includes the first racial mount, and gives 60% speed. Extra mount colours cost 20g each.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: The first mount comes from a free quest at your race's mount vendor after you learn Apprentice Riding. In Elwynn this is "Your First Horse" from Katie Hunter.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Journeyman Riding at level 60 costs 1,000g and gives 100% speed. Epic "Swift" mounts cost 200g each, so the minimum is about 1,200g before discounts.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Honored with your home faction gives 10% off riding and racial mounts, so the level-40 package costs 90g. Do not assume a further PvP-rank discount to 80g.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: The Legacy talent Bartering gives up to 10% off mounts but not riding training. Blizzard's beta fix confirms Bartering is not meant to discount training or repairs.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Mounts of other races need Exalted reputation with that race.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Paladins and Warlocks get their level-40 mount free through a class quest. The Alliance Paladin quest is "The Tome of Nobility"; the Horde/Forsaken Paladin version was not tested. Warlocks use Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. Their epic class-mount chains need reagents worth hundreds of gold.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Dual specialization unlocks at level 40. Its price is reported as 50g by MeinMMO, an Icy Veins snippet and the wiki patch page. Other guides say no price was announced.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: A realistic level-40 budget is about 150g: 100g riding plus 50g dual spec, plus new class ranks.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: At level 60, plan for well over 1,000g to cover the fast mount plus skills, repairs, consumables and respecs.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Training every class ability from 1 to 60 costs about 206–207g for every class. Abilities learned at the same level usually cost the same, and Warlock training was made cheaper to offset buying pet Grimoires.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Talent respecs cost 1 silver in the beta, with the price rising after each respec and decaying after about an hour. Live respec pricing was not stated.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: The Black Market in Powderfuse Port (Riverglades) sells the Gift of Galloping for 150g: level 60, Bind-on-Pickup, +10% mounted speed for 360 hours. A beta version called "Steed's Gift" (15 days) was reported. This is a gold sink, not something a leveller needs.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: The Tauren racial Plainsrunning briefly gave +3% mounted speed (16 Oct) and lost it again on 26 Oct. Older guides may still cite the bonus.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: There are no flying mounts.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: In Classic, riding at 40 cost 20g for the skill plus 80g for the mount. Honored gave 10% off and PvP Rank 3 another 10%, so 80g with both.

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: In Classic, the epic mount cost 1,000g in total (commonly split as 900g skill plus 100g mount; Blizzard Watch's split differs).

statements.title: Gold milestones: mount, riding, dual spec, class training
statements.text: Classic forum anecdotes put gold on hand at level 40 anywhere from about 95g (just enough for the mount) to more than 250g (for players who sold every grey and farmed). Several posters say that simply continuing to level earns gold faster than stopping to farm.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Forever has no named realms. There is one Auction House per region, ruleset (Normal, PvP, RP, RP-PvP) and faction. Oceanic players reportedly share the US Auction House.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Faction Auction Houses are in Stormwind, Ironforge, Darnassus, Orgrimmar, Undercity and Thunder Bluff. An in-game test on 16 Nov found they are not cross-faction.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The neutral Auction House ("Blackwater" in the client) is in Gadgetzan, Booty Bay and Everlook. A price tracker treats Alliance, Horde and Blackwater as three separate markets. An auctioneer at Valanaar (Zephras Isle) is unverified.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The cut is 5% at faction Auction Houses and 15% at neutral ones. Neutral deposits are 5× the faction deposit.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Auction durations are 2, 8 or 24 hours. The faction deposit is 5%, 20% or 60% of the item's vendor sell price for those durations. These are Classic percentages, not verified on Forever.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The deposit is refunded only if the item sells. If an auction expires or is cancelled, the deposit is lost.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Sale gold is meant to arrive by mail 60 minutes after the sale.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: When selling, the seller receives the winning bid × (1 − cut) plus the refunded deposit.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Cancelling an auction with no bid loses the deposit. Cancelling one that has a bid loses the deposit and also charges the cut on the current bid.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Bids are held in escrow and cannot be cancelled.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The neutral deposit is 25%, 100% or 300% of vendor price for 2, 8 or 24 hours (5× faction). A Wowhead Classic snippet gives 75% and 150% instead.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The 12/24/48-hour retail durations and deposits must not be used for Forever.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The Black Market Auction House (Madame Swyndle, Powderfuse Port, Riverglades) is bid-only, so players cannot list items. Lots open at 100g (pets, toys, tabards) or 400g (Dungeon Set 1 pieces).

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: In the beta, a goblin named Mister Graphed (Riverglades) sold Black Lotus and Arcane Crystal for 50g each, with unlimited stock, plus other materials. On live he reportedly sells Pristine Leather for 5g, against about 5 silver on the player Auction House, so always check the AH first.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: The Auction House UI shows item suffixes and an equippable-level column.

statements.title: Auction House basics
statements.text: Mail to another character costs 30 copper per item. Mail between characters on the same account is instant, and unopened mail lasts 30 days.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: Gather along the route you are already questing instead of detouring for single nodes.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: Skinning is the recommended early money profession. It only needs a knife, and leather sells to vendors for silver per stack while early herbs and ore vendor for less.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: Grey items in higher-level zones vendor for a few gold each, so loot everything.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: Unbound blue and epic world drops can sell for hundreds of gold, so don't equip an unbound item you might sell. Forever adds hundreds of new drops from rare creatures.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: XP buff food is a sellable product because cooked food grants an XP bonus. Engineers' grenades are sellable because non-engineers can use them. Sharpening stones are also sellable.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: To save money while levelling: buy only the class ranks you use, delay levelling crafting professions, and get bags early.

statements.title: General (forever)
statements.text: Gold from quests rises sharply from level 48, because most quests at 48+ now pay gold (ECO-01 #1).

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Linen drops from humanoids up to about level 15. Examples: Elwynn kobolds, Westfall, Deadmines, Ragefire Chasm, Durotar Burning Blade.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Wool drops from humanoids of about levels 15–36, best around 20–23. Examples: Stockade, Shadowfang Keep, Blackfathom Deeps, Duskwood ogres, Wetlands Mosshide and Dragonmaw, Ashenvale Thistlefur.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Silk drops from humanoids of about levels 25–41. Examples: Scarlet Monastery, Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs, Uldaman, Gnomeregan, Stromgarde, Stranglethorn Bloodscalp trolls, Dustwallow Grimtotem.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Mageweave drops from humanoids of about levels 40–52. Examples: Felwood Deadwood furbolgs, Searing Gorge, Badlands, Tanaris, Hinterlands Witherbark trolls, Zul'Farrak, Sunken Temple.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Runecloth drops from humanoids of about levels 51–60. Examples: Blackrock Depths, Blackrock Spire, Dire Maul, Scholomance, Stratholme, Silithus, Felwood, Azshara, the Plaguelands, Winterspring.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Felcloth drops from demons of about levels 53–54 (Felwood Jadefire, Azshara Legashi, Blasted Lands, Dire Maul), at roughly 1 in 15–20.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: Bag recipes now need more cloth: Red Mageweave Bag 5 bolts (was 4), Green Silk Pack 5 (was 4), Black Silk Pack 6 (was 5), Green and Red Woolen Bag 5 (was 4). This raises demand for cloth.

statements.title: Cloth and materials by level; Forever AH snapshot
statements.text: First Aid now makes healing potions, which adds herb demand (for example Peacebloom, Bruiseweed, Golden Sansam).

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Only green, blue and epic armour and weapons can be disenchanted. Reputation-vendor gear and tabards cannot.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Green armour mostly gives dust (about 75%). Green weapons mostly give essence (about 75%). There is about a 5% shard chance from item level 16 upward.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text:
Green items, by item level:
– 5–15: Strange Dust or Lesser Magic Essence
– 16–20: Strange Dust or Greater Magic Essence
– 21–25: Strange Dust or Lesser Astral Essence (Small Glimmering Shard possible)
– 26–30: Soul Dust or Greater Astral Essence (Large Glimmering Shard possible)
– 31–35: Soul Dust or Lesser Mystic Essence (Small Glowing Shard possible)
– 36–40: Vision Dust or Greater Mystic Essence (Large Glowing Shard possible)
– 41–45: Vision Dust or Lesser Nether Essence (Small Radiant Shard possible)
– 46–50: Dream Dust or Greater Nether Essence (Large Radiant Shard possible)
– 51–55: Dream Dust or Lesser Eternal Essence (Small Brilliant Shard possible)
– 56–65: Illusion Dust or Greater Eternal Essence (Large Brilliant Shard possible)

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Blue items give one shard: item level ≤25 Small Glimmering, 26–30 Large Glimmering, 31–35 Small Glowing, 36–40 Large Glowing, 41–45 Small Radiant, 46–50 Large Radiant, 51–55 Small Brilliant, 56–65 Large Brilliant (0.5% chance of a Nexus Crystal).

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Epic items give 2–4 shards (Radiant or Brilliant, depending on item level). From item level 56 they give a Nexus Crystal.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text:
Whether disenchanting needs a minimum Enchanting skill is disputed.
– One wiki page says vanilla had no skill requirement and that minimums arrived in patch 2.0.1. A Blizzard forum answer says Classic Era has no requirement.
– Another wiki page gives a skill-by-item-level table: item level ≤20 needs 1, 21–25 needs 25, then +25 per 5 item levels up to 56–60 needing 200.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: In Forever, disenchanting gives Enchanting skill-ups from skill 2 to 20. The chance drops after 20 and stops at 60.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Tailoring pairs well with Enchanting because it produces gear to disenchant. Fishing crates are an extra source of items to disenchant.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: The Enchanting camp object Arcane Salvager uses a Runed Golden Rod (was Truesilver). Its disenchant bonus now also works for lower-level enchanters (10 Nov).

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Disenchant only when the expected Auction House value of the materials after the 5% cut beats the vendor price. Bind-on-Pickup drops can only be vendored or disenchanted, so disenchanting usually wins for an enchanter.

statements.title: Disenchanting value
statements.text: Many Enchanting items now vendor for very little: Minor Wizard Oil 1s, crafted wands 1c. Enchanting crafts are not a vendor-gold source.

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: No source covers gold farming in the new Forever dungeons (City of Dalaran, Excavation Site: Wetlands, Drowned City, Blackmaw Hold).

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: Excavation Site: Wetlands has 4 bosses, 3 of which drop loot, with gear for about levels 24–28. Its bosses drop camp blueprints: Relic Guardian drops the Mining Rock Garden and Shadetooth drops the Herbalism Greenhouse.

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: Since 9 Nov, dungeons are a mixed source of XP, crates and loot: kill XP is up 50% and Waylaid Crates and Craftsman's Writs can drop. Since 13 Nov, the Drowned City's non-boss mobs respawn after 2 hours (was 1).

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: Every dungeon drop was reviewed and hundreds were added. Unique boss items are Rare. Bind-on-Pickup Uncommon and Rare dungeon loot gives its appearance to all eligible looters.

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: Some Blacksmithing and Leatherworking recipes became random dungeon drops (1 Oct). Advanced "Blueprint" recipes drop from specific bosses. Shaper's Terrace bosses drop higher-level skinning materials (9 Nov).

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: Bosses in dungeons of level 55 and above drop Tarnished Undermine Reals, which are exchanged with Pix Xizzix in Booty Bay. A weekly Undermine Satchel at level 60 contains items that sell for 10–100g.

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: Heart of the Mountain in Blackrock Depths can now be looted more than once (a bug fix, not a farm).

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text:
Classic dungeon farms:
– Scarlet Monastery: dense mobs, good for cloth and greens.
– Zul'Farrak: called the best "pure gold" farm, with Thorium and mage AoE.
– Maraudon: works for pet and ranged classes.
– Stratholme Live: Righteous Orbs.
– Blackrock Depths: runecloth, Dark Iron, rogue pickpocketing.
– Shadowfang Keep: trash can drop blues.
– Stockade: wool.

statements.title: Dungeon loops for gold
statements.text: A Stockade clear takes about 20–30 minutes at level 50+ and yields about 60–80 Wool.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Hundreds of new rare-creature drops were added, and world-drop epics were improved. Bind-on-Equip drops (items that only bind when worn) can be resold, which makes rare-mob hunting a source of sellable gear.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Selling a Bind-on-Equip item to a vendor while its appearance is uncollected makes it soulbound, not account-bound (beta, 1 Oct).

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Several items changed binding: the Bronze Mace is now Bind-on-Equip (17 Nov). Swiftstrike Shot and Swiftfeather Arrow are no longer Bind-on-Pickup but stay unavailable until raids open (10 Nov).

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Sell greys and vendor trash often, but check white items first because some are reagents. Plate and weapons vendor for the most. When no quest reward is an upgrade, take the one with the highest sell price.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Low-level shoulder items can sell well early on the Auction House because few shoulders exist at low level.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Limited-supply vendor recipes disappear when bought and restock over time. Buyers pay a premium to avoid the trip, so they can be resold. Reputation recipes are unlimited but Bind-on-Pickup. No Forever list of limited-supply recipes was found.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: Chaining short flight hops can be cheaper than one long flight, and buying lower spell ranks saves gold when you are short.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: The Legacy talent Frequent Flier makes flights cheaper and faster, and Bartering lowers vendor purchase prices. Blizzard has published no numbers for either.

statements.title: BoE farming, vendor trash and vendor recipes
statements.text: The Legacy talent Reagent Economy removes the need to buy class reagents and makes tier-1 camp objects free of materials.

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: The new factions Azeroth Commerce Authority (Alliance) and Durotar Supply and Logistics (Horde) are a major source of profession activity and award Merchant's Favor.

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: Merchant's Favor (currency 3402) comes from filling crates and turning them in at Three Corners in Redridge (Alliance, about 10,73) or west of the Crossroads in the Barrens (Horde, about 42,34).

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: Example Merchant's Favor prices: tabard 200; profession title 1,000; Advertising License Application 1,200; Packmule Treat 1,500; Reins of the Pack Kodo 6,000. Favor also buys profession recipes, and higher recipes need more reputation and more Favor.

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: Waylaid Crates come from world drops and chests and can be bought on the Auction House. Players fill them with set materials and hand them in at the hubs (Marcy Baker for Alliance, Dokimi for Horde). Crate tiers are Apprentice and Journeyman at level 10, Expert at 20 and Artisan at 35. Favor buys recipes, a pet, a toy and the Pack Kodo, but not gold.

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: Craftsman's Writs are world-drop quests worth 75 or 125 reputation.

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: A 17 Nov fix stopped one Waylaid Crate conversion from paying an obsolete item.

statements.title: Profession factions, Merchant's Favor, Waylaid Crates, Writs
statements.text: Each of the six crafting professions has a 300-skill certification that unlocks an account-wide title. For Leatherworking it costs 1,000 Favor.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: There are 12 professions: 9 primary (Alchemy, Blacksmithing, Enchanting, Engineering, Herbalism, Leatherworking, Mining, Skinning, Tailoring) and 3 secondary (Cooking, First Aid, Fishing). A character can have 2 primaries plus all secondaries. The maximum skill is 300.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: There is no Jewelcrafting or Inscription. In the beta, a Dalaran jewellery shop had an "Apprentice Jeweler" who taught nothing, and stats-panel strings mention Inscription. Any future addition is speculation. Wowhead's Forever Jewelcrafting page returns 404.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text:
Rank structure:
– Apprentice: skill cap 75.
– Journeyman: trained at skill 50, character level 10, cap 150.
– Expert: trained at 125, level 20, cap 225.
– Artisan: trained at 200, level 35, cap 300. Artisan comes from special trainers or quests.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: Apprentice level requirement: Warcraft Tavern says level 1 for gathering and 5 for crafting. Zockify and wow-professions say there is no level requirement.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: Training costs per rank, without reputation discount, are listed as 10 / 5 / 50 / 5 with no units shown. The Classic pattern is 10c / 5s / 50s / 5g. One Forever guide states the Expert cost as 50s. No Blizzard source gives Forever training costs.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text:
Over 600 new recipes were promised. A client-data count on live 1.60.1 (17 Nov) finds 857 new, by profession as total/new:
– Alchemy 178/69, Blacksmithing 416/177, Enchanting 214/64, Engineering 237/72
– Leatherworking 479/238, Tailoring 398/164
– Cooking 123/42, First Aid 31/17
– Mining 17/5, Herbalism 3/3, Skinning 3/3, Fishing 3/3
Beta counts were 861 and 884.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text:
Each profession has 3 camp objects. The first unlocks at profession skill 20, and advanced ones come from Blueprints that drop from dungeon bosses.
– A Basic Campfire holds 3 objects, one per player. Cooks can learn campfires holding 5 or 10.
– Camp buffs last 1 hour, need you to sit and rest at the fire, and do not stack with the class buff they mimic.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: A starting-zone quest offers Mining, Herbalism or Skinning as a reward, with +2 starting skill. Each starting zone has a Junior gathering trainer who teaches only up to 75 (and no smelting).

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: Each profession has its own crafting window with search, filters and Create All, plus a dedicated reagent-bag slot. Bags no longer equip themselves (launch notes).

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: Primary professions can be unlearned from the Professions window; secondary professions cannot.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: No profession gives a passive stat bonus: Mining gives no Stamina and Skinning gives no crit.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: Each crafting profession grants 1 Legacy point at skill 150, 225 and 300. Each character can spend up to 16 Legacy points at launch, and up to 65 can be earned in total.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text:
Profession-related Legacy talents (official names, no numbers):
– Working Overtime: higher skill-up chance.
– Bountiful Harvest: more Scarce resources.
– Bartering: cheaper vendor purchases.
– Performance: bonus Merchant's Favor.
– Master Chef: extra cooking results.
– Luremaster: extra fish.
– Dedicated Study: a daily skill boost, or Elemental Essences once all professions are at 300.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: Guides disagree on the Legacy talent numbers. Bountiful Harvest is +20% per rank to +100%, or "doubles at rank 1". Working Overtime is a flat +10% or 4–20%.

statements.title: Profession system rules (Forever)
statements.text: The 1.60.1 client added skill-line APIs and a categorised trainer window.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Scarce materials have no nodes of their own. They come as a chance bonus when gathering a normal node or skinning a corpse.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text:
There are nine, by tier:
– Mining: Pyrite, Bauxite, Pitchblende.
– Herbalism: Frilled Lichen, Rosecap, Stranglevine.
– Skinning: Pristine Leather, Pristine Hide, Pristine Scale.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Blizzard's only official mention of "Scarce resources" is the Bountiful Harvest talent text.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: No drop rate is published for any Scarce material.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text:
Pyrite (item 249391) stacks to 20 and vendors for 1s. It is a reagent for:
– Alchemy: Sulfuric Acid.
– Enchanting: Weapon – Insight, Weapon – Recovery, Necklace – Healing Power, Glimmering Staff.
– Engineering: 9-60 Battery Pack.
– Tailoring: the Shining and Filigreed gear.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Frilled Lichen (item 249399) drops from herb nodes from Earthroot (15) to Kingsblood (125), but not Grave Moss. It is used in Cerulean Dye (Alchemy: 2 Lichen + 1 Empty Vial, skill colours 40/50/70/90), which feeds Tailoring, Leatherworking and Enchanting. It is also used in Enchant Weapon – Insight.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Pristine Leather (item 249427) stacks to 20 and vendors for 1s25c. It is a reagent in 126 Blacksmithing, Leatherworking and Tailoring recipes, the most of any Scarce material.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text:
Pristine Leather appears in levelling-range recipes:
– Blacksmithing: chain belts at 85 (2 each), boots at 115 (4), Silvered Chain pieces at 125–155 (4–6).
– Tailoring: Filigreed Pristine Gown at 80 (2).
– Leatherworking: sets at 90–150 (2–8) and 195–270 (1–5).

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Pristine Scale (item 249429) vendors for 3s75c and is used in high-level recipes (Dragonscale pieces, Bottomless bags, Ultralight Goblin Glider, Timbermaw Tunic, among others).

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Recipe counts by material: Pristine Hide 46, Pristine Scale 16, Pyrite 15, Bauxite 2, Pitchblende 2 (including Smelt Azerothium), and 2 each for the herb Scarce materials.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Scarce-material dyes and reagents: Sulfuric Acid (2 Pyrite, skill 50), Cerulean Dye (2 Frilled Lichen, 50), Magenta Dye (2 Rosecap, 130), Viridian Dye (2 Stranglevine, 230).

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Which ores drop Scarce materials is disputed. One guide says Pyrite comes from Copper, Tin and Iron, Bauxite from Mithril, and Pitchblende from Thorium. Others say "most ore nodes", or put Bauxite on Iron and Mithril.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Herb mapping: Rosecap comes from Liferoot through Purple Lotus and Stranglevine from Sungrass through Icecap. Peacebloom, Silverleaf, Grave Moss, Arthas' Tears and Black Lotus give none.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: A community beta test suggests tier-1 Scarce materials (Pristine Leather, Frilled Lichen) stop dropping for characters above about level 25–26. Blizzard has not confirmed this.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Wowhead's Forever item pages reportedly say Pyrite and Pristine Leather "can be purchased in Riverglades". This fits the Mister Graphed vendor in Riverglades (ECO-03 #15) but needs checking in game.

statements.title: Scarce materials (Forever-only)
statements.text: Advice for Blacksmithing, Leatherworking and Tailoring levellers: skin as you go or plan to buy Pristine Leather.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Ore node skill requirements (orange): Copper 1, Tin 65, Silver 75, Iron 125, Gold 155, Mithril 175, Truesilver and Dark Iron 230, Small Thorium 245 (250 in a Classic source), Rich Thorium 275. Heavy Thorium Ore (new) needs 300 and is a rare spawn in Mount Hyjal.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: The general Classic skill-up pattern is orange at the requirement, yellow at +25, green at +50 and grey at +100 (for example Copper 1/25/50/100). Forever keeps the Classic gathering skill-up behaviour.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Ore stacks to 20 (was 10).

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Fewer Poor Copper Vein nodes spawn in starter areas. Starter areas have low-tier nodes (Poor Copper Vein, Teldrassil Chunk of Amber) that only give skill-ups to 20.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Nodes respawn much faster than in Classic, and spawn rates scale with the number of players nearby. Respawns are fastest in starting zones and slow as characters level, and Blizzard plans to slow low-level zones later.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Incendicite Ore in the Wetlands respawns faster and more evenly (beta). Spectral Iron Ore spawns more often and can be tracked (17 Nov).

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: A Mining Pick must be carried in your bags. It is sold by trade-goods and mining-supply vendors.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Smelting raises Mining skill. A cheap route from 1 to about 105 is: Copper Bar to 65, Tin Bar to 75, then Bronze Bar to 105, using about 140 Copper Ore and 70 Tin Ore. Optional steps are Silver (105–120), Iron (to about 135) and Gold (to about 175).

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text:
There are two new smelts, both learned at any Mining trainer:
– Azerothium Bar: Mining 275, 2 Pitchblende + 1 Coal.
– Heavy Thorium Bar: Mining 300, needs the Molten Foundry camp object or a dungeon forge.
Alchemists can transmute Heavy Thorium into Legionite.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text:
Levelling route by skill:
– 1–65: starting zones.
– 65–125: Wetlands (best), Silverpine, Hillsbrad, Westfall, Barrens, Ashenvale, Stonetalon.
– 125–175: Thousand Needles or Arathi.
– 175–245: Hinterlands, Tanaris.
– 245–275: Un'Goro, Blasted Lands, Felwood.
– 275–300: Un'Goro, Eastern Plaguelands, Winterspring, Burning Steppes.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text:
Mining trainers (all full trainers teach up to Artisan):
– Horde: Makaru (Orgrimmar), Brek Stonehoof (Thunder Bluff), Brom Killian (Undercity), Krunn (Razor Hill), Johan Focht (The Sepulcher).
– Alliance: Gelman Stonehand (Stormwind), Geofram Bouldertoe (Ironforge), Kurdram Stonehammer (Auberdine; Darnassus has none), Yarr Hammerstone (Dun Morogh), Matt Johnson (Darkshire), Brock Stoneseeker (Thelsamar).
– Neutral and new zones: Pikkle (Gadgetzan), Grungle (Powderfuse Port), Halavuul Cragwind (Valanaar), Messana Crestwind (Shen'dar).

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Items that add Mining skill: Enchant Gloves +2/+5, Goblin Mining Helmet +5, Miner's Cape +2 (Deadmines), Twilight Mine Light +4 (Alliance quest, Riverglades).

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: The Rockslicer (from Rhahk'Zor in the Deadmines) lets you mine low-level ore without the profession, for 30 uses.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Mining camp objects: Lodestone (skill 20), Rock Garden (140; blueprint from Relic Guardian, Excavation Site: Wetlands) and Molten Foundry (300). Their buff is like Blessing of Might.

statements.title: Mining (incl. smelting)
statements.text: Find Minerals and Find Herbs cannot run at the same time, but either can run alongside other tracking. Tracking turns off when you die.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text:
Herb skill requirements (orange):
– 1: Peacebloom, Silverleaf
– 15–125: Earthroot 15, Mageroyal 50, Briarthorn 70, Stranglekelp 85, Bruiseweed 100, Wild Steelbloom 115, Grave Moss 120, Kingsblood 125
– 150–245: Liferoot 150, Fadeleaf 160, Goldthorn 170, Khadgar's Whisker 185, Wintersbite 195, Firebloom 205, Purple Lotus 210, Arthas' Tears 220, Sungrass 230, Blindweed 235, Ghost Mushroom 245
– 250–300: Gromsblood 250, Golden Sansam 260, Dreamfoil 270, Mountain Silversage 280, Plaguebloom 285, Icecap 290, Black Lotus 300

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: Herbs turn green 15 points later than in Classic: at the requirement +65 instead of +50 (for example Peacebloom is 1/25/65/100).

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: No tool is needed.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: New endgame herbs are Marefoil, Demonsage and Death Lotus. Death Lotus comes from any Mount Hyjal herb when you have Enchant Gloves – Lotus Claw.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: Herb nodes also drop seeds, used in the Greenhouse and Seed Hybridizer camp objects.

The Tauren Cultivation racial duplicates a nearby herb. It needs character level of at least the herb's skill requirement ÷ 5 and has a 15-minute cooldown. It works on Mageroyal (17 Nov fix) and Purple Lotus (19 Nov fix), and since 19 Nov it succeeds more reliably on herbs you have the Herbalism skill for.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: Starting zones have low-tier herb nodes (Wilted Peacebloom, Stunted Silverleaf) that only give skill-ups to 20.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text:
Levelling route by skill:
– 1–70: starting zones.
– 70–115: Silverpine, Loch Modan, Darkshore.
– 115–170: Hillsbrad, Stonetalon.
– 170–205: Stranglethorn, Arathi.
– 205–230: Tanaris, Searing Gorge (train Artisan first).
– 230–270: Hinterlands.
– 270–300: Felwood.
Note: beyond 170 the route is copied from Classic, because the beta capped at level 30.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text:
Herbalism trainers:
– Horde: Jandi (Orgrimmar), Komin Winterhoof (Thunder Bluff), Martha Alliestar (Undercity), Mishiki (Sen'jin), Faruza (Brill), Aranae Venomblood (Tarren Mill), Ruw (Camp Mojache), Angrun (Grom'gol).
– Alliance: Tannysa and Shylamiir (Stormwind), Reyna Stonebranch (Ironforge), Firodren Mooncaller (Darnassus), Malorne Bladeleaf (Dolanaar), Herbalist Pomeroy (Elwynn), Kali Healtouch (Thelsamar), Alma Jainrose (Lakeshire), Telurinon Moonshadow (Menethil), Cylania Rootstalker (Ashenvale), Brant Jasperbloom (Theramore).
– Neutral: Flora Silverwind (Booty Bay), Malvor (Moonglade), and two trainers on Zephras Isle.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: Items that add Herbalism skill: Enchant Gloves +2/+5, Herbalist's Gloves +5, Bog Pickers +5 (Wetlands drop), Apothecary Gloves +2 (Horde quest), Goldthorn Tea +15. A 12-slot Herb Pouch costs 10s from a vendor, and herbs go into the reagent-bag slot first.

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: Herbalism camp objects: Incense Candle (skill 20, an Intellect buff like Arcane Intellect), Greenhouse (140; blueprint from Shadetooth, Excavation Site: Wetlands) and Seed Hybridizer (300).

statements.title: Herbalism
statements.text: Druids can herb in Travel Form without leaving it. This is unverified and was not possible in Classic.

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Skill needed to skin a mob: 1 for mob levels 1–10; (level − 10) × 10 for levels 11–20; level × 5 for level 21 and up, so a level-60 mob needs 300. This is the same as Classic.

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Each creature can only be skinned once (beta change).

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: A Skinning Knife (item 7005) must be in your bags. Horde can get the Keen Skinning Knife (+3) from the quest "Unwelcome Guests" in the Barrens.

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Fel Leather and Fel Hide are new skinnable materials, plus the Scarce Pristine Leather, Hide and Scale (PRF-00b).

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text:
Levelling route by skill:
– 1–75: starting zone.
– 75–150: Barrens (mobs 16–18) or Loch Modan, then Wetlands Whelgar's Excavation (25–27).
– 150–225: Hillsbrad yetis (30–32) or Duskwood worgen.
– 225–280: Feralas Feral Scar Vale (43–46).
– 280–300: Un'Goro (50–55).

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text:
Skinning trainers:
– Horde: Thuwd (Orgrimmar), Mooranta (Thunder Bluff), Killian Hagey (Undercity), Yonn Deepcut (Bloodhoof), Rand Rhobart (Tirisfal), Dranh (Camp Taurajo), Malux (Shadowprey), Kulleg Stonehorn (Camp Mojache).
– Alliance: Maris Granger (Stormwind), Balthus Stoneflayer (Ironforge), Eladriel (Darnassus), Helene Peltskinner (Goldshire; she teaches even while you hold her quest), Radnaal Maneweaver (Teldrassil), Wilma Ranthal (Redridge), Jayla (Ashenvale).
– Zephras Isle: two trainers.

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Items that add Skinning skill: Enchant Gloves – Skinning +5 (Enchanting 200), Advanced Skinning +10 (Enchanting 250), Cartilage Shapers +4.

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Skinning camp objects: Camp Chair (skill 20, +2% crit like Moonkin Aura), Field Guide (140; blueprint from Lady Anacondra in Wailing Caverns; teaches Track Beasts) and Trapper's Workbench (300).

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Shaper's Terrace bosses drop higher-level skinning materials (9 Nov).

statements.title: Skinning
statements.text: Skinning is fastest on mobs you already kill while questing rather than on dedicated trips, since melee classes and hunters skin their own kills.

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text:
Ranks:
– Apprentice and Journeyman from any fishing trainer (Journeyman at skill 50, level 10).
– Expert from the book "Expert Fishing – The Bass and You", sold by Old Man Heming in Booty Bay for 1g (skill 125, level 20).
– Artisan from the quest "Nat Pagle, Angler Extreme", given by Nat Pagle (Dustwallow Marsh; skill 225, level 35).

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text: The Artisan quest needs four fish: Feralas Ahi, Misty Reed Mahi Mahi (Swamp of Sorrows), Sar'theris Striker (Desolace) and Savage Coast Blue Sailfin (Stranglethorn).

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text:
Levelling route by skill:
– 1–75: starting zones, using a Shiny Bauble lure.
– 75–150: capitals, Barrens, Darkshore, Loch Modan, Westfall, Silverpine.
– 150–225: Dustwallow, Arathi, Desolace, Stranglethorn, Swamp of Sorrows, Thousand Needles.
– 225–300: Felwood, Feralas, Hinterlands, Tanaris, Un'Goro, Western Plaguelands.

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text: Poles: Strong Fishing Pole +5, Blump Family pole +3 (Alliance), Ravaged Fishing Pole +15 (new; from Lord Angler in Dustwallow), Big Iron +20, Nat Pagle's pole +25 (Horde), Arcanite +35. Lures add +25 to +100.

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text: Forever adds uncommon and rare fish (the Fishing Rack and Hut camp objects help catch them) and fish foods that give temporary Fishing skill (+3 to +18). The Stranglethorn Fishing Extravaganza now rewards the first 50 players per event.

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text:
Fishing trainers:
– Horde: Lumak (Orgrimmar), Kah Mistrunner (Thunder Bluff), Armand Cromwell (Undercity), Lau'Tiki (Sen'jin), Uthan Stillwater (Mulgore), Clyde Kellen (Tirisfal), Kil'Hiwana (Zoram'gar), Lui'Mala (Shadowprey), Katoom the Angler (Revantusk).
– Alliance: Arnold Leland (Stormwind), Grimnur Stonebrand (Ironforge), Astaia (Darnassus), Lee Brown (Elwynn), Paxton Ganter (Dun Morogh), Androl Oakhand (Rut'theran), Harold Riggs (Menethil), Warg Deepwater (Loch Modan), Matthew Hooper (Redridge), Donald Rabonne (Southshore), Brannock (Feathermoon).
– Neutral: Myizz Luckycatch (Booty Bay), Krix (Powderfuse Port), and Zephras Isle trainers.

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text: Fishing camp objects: Fish Bowl (skill 20, like Blessing of Kings at 8%), Fishing Rack (140; blueprint from Gelihast in Blackfathom Deeps) and Fishing Hut (300).

statements.title: Fishing
statements.text: "Master Angler" is a datamined title.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text: Cooked food gives a small XP bonus plus stats (official). Guides specify the Well Fed buff as +5% XP from kills, not quests, lasting about 15 minutes and lost on death. Only one food buff can be active at a time.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text:
Ranks:
– Apprentice and Journeyman from a trainer.
– Expert from the Expert Cookbook, 1g, sold by Wulan (Shadowprey, Horde) or Shandrina (Silverwind Refuge, Alliance), at skill 125.
– Artisan from the quest "Clamlette Surprise" from Dirge Quikcleave in Gadgetzan (skill 225, level 35). It needs 12 Giant Egg, 10 Zesty Clam Meat and 20 Alterac Swiss.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text: Cooking teaches the Basic Campfire Kit, which is the hub of the camping system. Cooks can learn larger campfires. The Journeyman Campfire Kit needs Cooking 90 (was 140, changed 10 Nov).

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text:
Recipe changes:
– Most foods now favour one primary stat.
– Longjaw Mud Snapper and Smoked Sagefish give attack power or spell power.
– Bristle Whisker Catfish gives Fishing skill.
– New dishes: Plated Armorfish and Savory Whimsyfin Delight (Whimsyfin from Redridge).
– Cookie's Stirring Rod (Deadmines) gives +25% cooking speed.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text:
Levelling route by skill:
– 1–50: smallfish, wolf and boar.
– 50–100: Longjaw, Rainbow Fin, bear meat, Strider Stew.
– 100–175: Catfish, Crab Claw (Alliance), Hot Lion Chops (Horde), omelets, clams.
– 175–225: Roast Raptor, Mithril Headed Trout, Soothing Turtle Bisque.
– 225–300: about 140 Spotted Yellowtail or Filet of Redgill.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text:
Cooking trainers:
– Horde: Zamja (Orgrimmar), Aska Mistrunner (Thunder Bluff), Eunice Burch (Undercity), Cook Torka (Razor Hill), Pyall Silentstride (Bloodhoof), William Pickman (Brill), Duhng (Barrens), Mudduk (Grom'gol), Gorg (Rog'mar, Riverglades).
– Alliance: Stephen Ryback (Stormwind), Daryl Riknussun (Ironforge), Alegorn (Darnassus), Tomas (Goldshire), Gremlock Pilsnor (Kharanos), Cook Ghilm (Gol'Bolar), Zarrin (Dolanaar), Crystal Boughman (Lakeshire), Katherine Lee (Dalaran, Alterac).
– Zephras Isle: Nyalah Brightfire, who sells more supplies since 13 Nov.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text: The Legacy talents Master Chef (chance of extra results) and Gourmand (longer-lasting food) apply.

statements.title: Cooking
statements.text: Mild Spices now sell to vendors for 1c (5 Nov).

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text: Healing potions moved from Alchemy to First Aid. The six are Minor (skill 1), Lesser (55), Healing (110), Greater (155), Superior (215) and Major (275), and they now also need spices. First Aid also has Poison, Disease and Bleed cures.

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text:
Ranks:
– Apprentice and Journeyman from a trainer.
– Expert from the book "Expert First Aid – Under Wraps", 1g, skill 125, no level requirement. Sold by Deneb Walker (Stromgarde, Arathi) for Alliance or Balai Lok'Wein (Brackenwall, Dustwallow) for Horde.
– Artisan from the quest "Triage" (skill 225, level 35), from Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen (Theramore) for Alliance or Doctor Gregory Victor (Hammerfall) for Horde.

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text: Bandage route by skill (Wowhead): Linen 1–40, Heavy Linen 40–80, Wool 80–115, Heavy Wool 115–150, Silk 150–180, Heavy Silk 180–210, Mageweave 210–240, Heavy Mageweave 240–260, Runecloth 260–290, Heavy Runecloth 290–300. Cloth totals: about 151 Linen, 144 Wool, 123 Silk, 89 Mageweave, 62 Runecloth.

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text: An alternative route saves cloth by mixing in potions: about 86 Minor Healing Potions for 1–75, Simple Poultice and Healing Potion in the middle, and about 30 Major Healing Potions for 275–300. The Major Healing Potion manual is sold by Pexmit (Mount Hyjal) for 8g; Horde can also get it as a quest reward.

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text:
First Aid trainers:
– Horde: Arnok (Orgrimmar), Pand Stonebinder (Thunder Bluff), Mary Edras (Undercity), Rawrk (Razor Hill), Vira Younghoof (Bloodhoof), Nurse Neela (Brill).
– Alliance: Shaina Fuller (Stormwind), Nissa Firestone (Ironforge), Dannelor (Darnassus), Michelle Belle (Goldshire), Thamner Pol (Kharanos), Byancie (Dolanaar), Fremal Doohickey (Wetlands), Angelique Butler (Dalaran).
– Zephras Isle: two trainers.

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text: First Aid camp objects: First Aid Kit (skill 20, a Stamina buff like Power Word: Fortitude), Toxin Study and Plague Doctor's Laboratory.

statements.title: First Aid
statements.text: Because healing potions are now in First Aid, a character does not need Alchemy for healing potions.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: Alchemy no longer makes the standard healing potions. Instead it has a "Discolored Healing Potion" line, which heals but has a side effect. Major Discolored Healing Potion is unlocked by a short questline from Odd Child (Westfall, Alliance) or Apothecary Renferrel (Silverpine, Horde).

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text:
New or changed recipes:
– Minor Arcane Elixir: low-level spell power. It now vendors for 5c.
– Elixir of the Grizzly: Strength and crit.
– Elixir of Cunning: Agility and Intellect, aimed at hunters.
– Rage Potion: now usable by druids.
– Alchemists can also make dyes.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: Camp objects are the Mana Well, Fermenter and Alchemy Laboratory, which buff like Blessing of Wisdom. The portable Laboratory lets you make flasks anywhere, without going to Scholomance.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: Some recipes were renamed: Elixir of Defense is now Elixir of Lesser Defense, and Elixir of Detect Demon and Catseye Elixir are now "Draughts". Transmutes from Iron to Gold and from Mithril to Truesilver reportedly have a 1-hour cooldown.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: Draught of Predatory Senses now shares the potion cooldown.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text:
Route A (Wowhead, about 316 crafts), by skill:
– 1–12: Elixir of Minor Force
– 12–55: Elixir of Minor Defense
– 55–65: Minor Mana Potion
– 65–90: Elixir of Minor Fortitude
– 90–120: Elixir of Wisdom
– 120–160: Lesser Mana Potion
– 160–195: Mana Potion
– 195–205: Elixir of Agility
– 205–240: Greater Mana Potion
– 225: Philosopher's Stone (from Alchemist Pestlezugg; keep it)
– 240–260: Draught of Detect Undead
– 260–270: Superior Mana Potion (recipe from Ulthir for Alliance or Algernon for Horde)
– 270–300: Major Discolored Healing Potion
Main materials: about 163 Empty Vials, 88 Leaded Vials, 64 Crystal Vials, 91 Stranglekelp, 83 Mageroyal, 79 Peacebloom, 60 Briarthorn, 54 Silverleaf, 52 Earthroot, 50 Goldthorn, 40 Khadgar's Whisker, 38 Kingsblood, 31 Plaguebloom, 31 Murloc Eye, 23 Arthas' Tears, 20 Sungrass and 20 Blindweed.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: Route B (RankedBoost, about 388 crafts) uses Elixir of Minor Defense, Minor Mana, Swiftness and Holy Protection, then Lesser Mana, Elixir of Lesser Defense, Mana, Agility, Catseye Draught, Detect Undead and Detect Demon. Several recipe sources are unconfirmed for Forever (Swiftness, Holy Protection, Greater Arcane Protection).

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text:
Alchemy trainers:
– Alliance Apprentice: Stormwind, Ironforge, Darnassus, Elwynn, Dolanaar, Thelsamar, Zephras Isle.
– Alliance Journeyman: Lilyssia Nightbreeze (Stormwind), Tally Berryfizz (Ironforge), Alchemist Narett (Theramore), Kylanna (Ashenvale).
– Alliance Expert: Ainethil (Darnassus), or Linzy Blackbolt / Patricia Egan (Dalaran, Alterac).
– Alliance Artisan: Kylanna Windwhisper (Feathermoon, Feralas).
– Horde Apprentice: Whuut (Orgrimmar), Kray (Thunder Bluff), Doctor Martin Felben (Undercity), Miao'zan (Sen'jin), Carolai Anise (Brill).
– Horde Journeyman: Yelmak, Bena Winterhoof, Doctor Marsh, Serge Hinott (Tarren Mill).
– Horde Expert: Doctor Herbert Halsey (Undercity).
– Horde Artisan: Rogvar (Stonard).
– Neutral: Jaxin Chong (Booty Bay, Journeyman) and Master Mycologist Shurome (Felwood, Artisan).

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: Classic skill levels for useful consumables (check in game): Elixir of Lion's Strength 1, Minor Mana 25, Elixir of Minor Agility 50, Swiftness Potion 60, Lesser Mana 120, Elixir of Lesser Agility 140, Free Action 150, Mana Potion 160, Elixir of Agility 185, Elixir of Greater Agility 240.

statements.title: Alchemy
statements.text: The Classic route is not valid as-is on Forever because healing potions moved to First Aid. It ran healing potions from 1 to 230, then Detect Undead, Greater Agility, Superior Mana and Major Healing.

statements.title: Blacksmithing
statements.text: Many existing plans were buffed so their items stay useful earlier, and hundreds of new plans come from Merchant's Favor and dungeon or raid drops. They favour hybrid classes, with mail and plate sets. The wiki lists about 480 plans: roughly 52 Apprentice, 94 Journeyman, 112 Expert and 238 Artisan.

statements.title: Blacksmithing
statements.text: Sharpening Stones and Weightstones now stack with poisons, Windfury Weapon and Windfury Totem.

statements.title: Blacksmithing
statements.text: Camp objects are the Sharpening Wheel and Master Forge (a Strength/Agility buff like Strength of Earth Totem) and the Anvil.

statements.title: Blacksmithing
statements.text:
New sets and materials:
– Mail sets: Acolyte's, Crusader's, Guard's, Protector's, Veteran's.
– Plate sets: Enriched Thorium, Justicar's, Officer's, Prefect's, Sentinel's, Warder's.
– New materials: Azerothium Bar, Legionite Bar, Torbernite.
– The Mithril Scale pieces were renamed Mithril Plate.
– New Copper Rod plan; Silver Rods are reportedly no longer obtainable.

statements.title: Blacksmithing
statements.text:
Route A (RankedBoost, about 330–395 crafts), by skill:
– 1–44: Rough Sharpening Stone
– 44–75: Copper Chain Pants
– 75–95: Bronze Mace
– 95–140: Rough Bronze Leggings
– 140–155: Silvered Bronze Gauntlets
– 155–165: Bronze Warhammer
– 165–175: Green Iron Bracers
– 175–186: Truesilver Skeleton Key
– 186–200: Golden Scale Bracers
– 200–205: Heavy Mithril Gauntlet
– 205–217: Mithril Plate Pants
– 217–225: Mithril Spurs

statements.title: Blacksmithing
statements.text: Blacksmithing specialisation needs character level 40 and Blacksmithing 200. The choice is Armorsmith or Weaponsmith, and Weaponsmith later splits into Axe, Hammer or Sword. The pick is permanent unless you drop the profession and start over. These details are probably carried over from Classic, and one guide could not confirm them for Forever.

statements.text: New "Saf T" and "EZ-Thro" explosives can be used by non-engineers at any level and do not bind, so they are sellable. Examples: Saf T Dynamite, Saf T Copper Bomb, EZ-Thro Thorium Grenade, Dark Bomb, Mana Bomb, and the SAF-T Disposable Parachute.

statements.text:

statements.title: Engineering

statements.title: Engineering

statements.title: Enchanting
statements.text: Crafted wands gain spell power at level 5, but they no longer scale with your spell damage (beta change). Wands vendor for 1c.

statements.text:

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Cloth (Mage, Priest, Warlock): Tailoring plus Enchanting is the standard pair, because spare tailored gear disenchants into enchanting materials.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text:
Cloth: The Forever-specific self-crafts are:
– the school sets from PRF-12 #10 (Mage: Fire, Frost or Arcane; Warlock: Shadow or Fire; Priest: Healing, Holy or Shadow);
– the spell-power Azure Silk Hood and Woolen Shoulders;
– the Filigreed Pristine Gown (skill 80) and the Shining pieces (80–145, which use Pyrite);
– bags and reagent bags.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Cloth: Items on the Forever route worth wearing: Lesser Wizard's Robe and Robe of Power. Classic staples are Azure Silk Hood, the Black Mageweave set, Runecloth pieces, and the Soul Pouch for warlocks.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Casters (any): Crafted wands gain spell power at level 5. Minor Arcane Elixir (Alchemy) and the new Spell Power necklace enchant help casters.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Leather (Rogue, Druid; Hunter and Shaman before 40): Skinning plus Leatherworking is the default pair.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Leather: Forever adds class-themed leather sets in the levelling range. Matching by set name (compiler's inference): Prowler's, Skulker's and Brawler's suit rogues and feral druids; Mender's, Wisdom's, Totemic and Skycaller's suit druid and shaman casters; Trapper's and Stalker's suit hunters. Forceful and Mystic Armor Kits and the Light Leather Reagent Bag are also available.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Leather: Items on the route worth wearing: Embossed and Dark leather pieces, Barbaric Shoulders, Guardian Gloves, Nightscape pieces, and Armor Kits.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text:

– Blacksmithing chain belts (skill 85) and Silvered Chain pieces (125–155), which use Pristine Leather.
– Leatherworking Turtle Scale (Classic route) and Dragonscale (from skill 225 and level 40).
– New Blacksmithing mail sets aimed at hybrids (Acolyte's, Crusader's, Guard's, Protector's, Veteran's), whose exact levels are not documented.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Plate (Warrior, Paladin): Mining plus Blacksmithing is the levelling pair. Blacksmithing gives plate upgrades and stones, and the stones now stack with poisons and Windfury. New plate sets: Officer's, Sentinel's, Justicar's and others.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Melee (any): Sharpening stones and weightstones from Blacksmithing are worth crafting for yourself. Mithril Spurs, if obtainable on Forever, adds mount speed.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: All: Crafter-only armour from Blacksmithing, Leatherworking and Tailoring appears around levels 30–50 and replaces quest rewards. No source ranks these items against quest rewards for each class.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text:
All: Engineering:
– Satchel of Copper Bombs for ranged pulls without ammo.
– Bombs with an AoE stun.
– Scopes and ammo for hunters.
– The EZ-Thro grenades do not need Engineering to use, so non-engineers can buy them.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: All: First Aid supplies bandages and now healing potions, and Cooking supplies XP food. These are the self-crafts with the most universal value, and they do not use a primary profession slot.

statements.title: What to craft for yourself while levelling, by armour type and class
statements.text: Paladin, Shaman, Druid: Enchanting makes the librams, totems and idols for these classes.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Blizzard designed professions to be part of levelling: crafted food gives XP and stats, and camps give 1-hour buffs while you rest.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: The XP levers tied to professions are the Well Fed buff from food (+5% kill XP), the Leatherworking Camp Tent (rested XP), and the Legacy talent Well Rested (more rested XP and a higher rested cap).

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Don't chase nodes several minutes off your route. Keep your crafting skill close to your character level, otherwise the crafted items are outdated before you can use them. Choose your pair early, and don't fund two crafting professions on a first character.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Faster respawns and spawns that scale with player numbers make gathering along your route cheaper in time on Forever than in Classic.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Gathering costs only trainer fees (about 5.6g in total for 1–300) plus a tool, which makes it the cheapest money profession for a leveller.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: No Forever source says whether gathering gives character XP. Classic Era gives none, per one forum post.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Herbalism, Mining, Skinning and Leatherworking are easy to level alongside questing. Blacksmithing, Leatherworking and First Aid need significant farming.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Holding off on levelling crafting professions saves gold before level 40.

statements.title: Professions and levelling time
statements.text: Tier-1 Scarce materials may only drop for characters up to about level 25. If so, the 10–25 levelling window is when to gather them (unconfirmed).
At max level, quest experience is no longer converted to gold.
The Booty Bay level-60 weekly is In Demand - Ancient Elven Curiosities. Its Undermine Satchel holds one vendor item: Gold Nugget 10g, Huge Quartz Gem 20g, Silver Necklace 40g or Gold Ring 100g.
Spectral Iron Ore (Shen'dralas) can be tracked by miners and spawns more often; Bronze Mace is now bind-on-equip.
Faction Auction House deposits are 5% of the vendor price for 2 hours, 20% for 8 hours and 60% for 24 hours, with a 1-copper minimum (live from the 17 Nov weekly reset).
Pix Xizzix's level-60 weekly quest rotates between dungeons. One week needed Drakkisath and Wyrmthalak (Blackrock Spire) plus Emperor Thaurissan (BRD) instead of Dire Maul.
The Undermine Satchel can hold vendor items worth 10g (Gold Nugget), 20g (Huge Quartz Gem), 40g (Silver Necklace) or 100g (Gold Ring), plus crafting materials.

Blizzard confirmed that non-elite Blackmaw Hold mobs wrongly dropped elite-level loot, and a hotfix on 16 Nov fixed it. Deliberate farmers had their gold removed, and heavy abusers were suspended. Players who benefited by chance were not penalised.
The Seed Hybridizer camp object is usable again; combining seeds in it now has a chance to fail and gives adjusted results.
Scarce Herb Seeds cannot be used in the Seed Hybridizer.
